sanskrit: mahāhradaṃ samāsādya kāśyapas tapasi sthitaḥ dīrghakālaṃ pariśrānta ṛṣir devarṣisaṃmataḥ
english: Having approached the great lake, Kāśyapa stood fixed in ascetic practice; long-wearied was that sage, esteemed among the divine seers.

sanskrit: tasya retaḥ pracaskanda dṛṣṭvāpsarasam urvaśīm apsūpaspṛśato rājan mṛgī tac cāpibat tadā
english: His seed fell upon beholding the apsarā Urvaśī while he touched the waters, O king, and a doe drank it then.

sanskrit: saha toyena tṛṣitā sā garbhiṇy abhavan nṛpa amoghatvād vidheś caiva bhāvitvād daivanirmitāt
english: Thirsty, she drank it together with the water and became with child, O king — by the infallibility of fate and the inevitability of what was divinely ordained.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ mṛgyāṃ samabhavat tasya putro mahān ṛṣiḥ ṛśyaśṛṅgas taponityo vana eva vyavardhata
english: From that doe was born his great son, the sage Ṛśyaśṛṅga, ever devoted to austerity; he grew up in the forest itself.

sanskrit: tasyarśyaśṛṅgaṃ śirasi rājann āsīn mahātmanaḥ tenarśyaśṛṅga ity evaṃ tadā sa prathito 'bhavat
english: On the head of that great-souled one there was the horn of a deer, O king; hence he became known by the name Ṛśyaśṛṅga.

sanskrit: na tena dṛṣṭapūrvo 'nyaḥ pitur anyatra mānuṣaḥ tasmāt tasya mano nityaṃ brahmacarye 'bhavan nṛpa
english: No other person had ever been seen by him apart from his father; therefore his mind was always fixed in celibacy, O king.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu sakhā daśarathasya vai lomapāda iti khyāto aṅgānām īśvaro 'bhavat
english: At this very time, the lord of the Aṅgas who was known as Lomapāda, a friend of Daśaratha, ruled.

sanskrit: tena kāmaḥ kṛto mithyā brāhmaṇebhya iti śrutiḥ sa brāhmaṇaiḥ parityaktas tadā vai jagatīpatiḥ
english: By him a false promise had been made to brāhmaṇas — so the tradition goes; and that lord of the earth was then abandoned by the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: purohitāpacārāc ca tasya rājño yadṛcchayā na vavarṣa sahasrākṣas tato 'pīḍyanta vai prajāḥ
english: And on account of the wrong done to the royal priest, the thousand-eyed Indra did not send rain by chance; thereafter the people were greatly afflicted.

sanskrit: sa brāhmaṇān paryapṛcchat tapoyuktān manīṣiṇaḥ pravarṣaṇe surendrasya samarthān pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: That lord of the earth consulted the brāhmaṇas — the wise, endowed with austerity — who were capable of inducing the great Indra to send rain.

sanskrit: kathaṃ pravarṣet parjanya upāyaḥ paridṛśyatām tam ūcuś coditās tena svamatāni manīṣiṇaḥ
english: "How may the rain-cloud pour forth? Let a means be found." Thus prompted by him, the wise ones declared their own views.

sanskrit: tatra tv eko munivaras taṃ rājānam uvāca ha kupitās tava rājendra brāhmaṇā niskṛtiṃ cara
english: Then one foremost among sages said to that king: "The brāhmaṇas are angered with you, O king of kings; make atonement."

sanskrit: ṛśyaśṛṅgaṃ munisutam ānayasva ca pārthiva vāneyam anabhijñaṃ ca nārīṇām ārjave ratam
english: "Bring Ṛśyaśṛṅga, the son of the sage, O king — he who is forest-born, unacquainted with women, and devoted to uprightness."

sanskrit: sa ced avatared rājan viṣayaṃ te mahātapāḥ sadyaḥ pravarṣet parjanya iti me nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "If that great ascetic should descend into your kingdom, O king, the rain-cloud will pour forth immediately — of this I have no doubt."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco rājan kṛtvā niskṛtim ātmanaḥ sa gatvā punar āgacchat prasanneṣu dvijātiṣu rājānam āgataṃ dṛṣṭvā pratisaṃjagṛhuḥ prajāḥ
english: Hearing this counsel, O king, and having made atonement for himself, he went and returned; when the twice-born were appeased, the people, seeing the king had returned, welcomed him with joy.

sanskrit: tato 'ṅgapatir āhūya sacivān mantrakovidān ṛśyaśṛṅgāgame yatnam akaron mantraniścaye
english: Then the lord of the Aṅgas, summoning his ministers skilled in counsel, applied himself with effort to the settled plan for bringing Ṛśyaśṛṅga.

sanskrit: so 'dhyagacchad upāyaṃ tu tair amātyaiḥ sahācyutaḥ śāstrajñair alam arthajñair nītyāṃ ca pariniṣṭhitaiḥ
english: He, together with those ministers — fully versed in scripture, skilled in affairs, and thoroughly grounded in statecraft — devised a means.

sanskrit: tata ānāyayām āsa vāramukhyā mahīpatiḥ veśyāḥ sarvatra niṣṇātās tā uvāca sa pārthivaḥ
english: Then that lord of the earth summoned the foremost of courtesans — women expert in every art — and the king spoke to them thus:

sanskrit: ṛśyaśṛṅgam ṛṣeḥ putram ānayadhvam upāyataḥ lobhayitvābhiviśvāsya viṣayaṃ mama śobhanāḥ
english: "Bring Ṛśyaśṛṅga, the son of the sage, by stratagem — enticing him, winning his trust, and drawing him into my kingdom, O lovely ones."

sanskrit: tā rājabhayabhītāś ca śāpabhītāś ca yoṣitaḥ aśakyam ūcus tat kāryaṃ vivarṇā gatacetasaḥ
english: Those women, fearing the king and fearing the curse, declared the task impossible, pale-faced and dispirited.

sanskrit: tatra tv ekā jaradyoṣā rājānam idam abravīt prayatiṣye mahārāja tam ānetuṃ tapodhanam
english: Then one aged woman among them said this to the king: "I will endeavour, great king, to bring that treasure-house of austerity."

sanskrit: abhipretāṃs tu me kāmān samanujñātum arhasi tataḥ śakṣye lobhayituṃ ṛśyaśṛṅgam ṛṣeḥ sutam
english: "You must grant the desires I have in mind; then I shall be able to entice Ṛśyaśṛṅga, the son of the sage."

sanskrit: tasyāḥ sarvam abhiprāyam anvajānāt sa pārthivaḥ dhanaṃ ca pradadau bhūri ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: That king agreed to her entire intention, and gave her abundant wealth and various jewels.

sanskrit: tato rūpeṇa saṃpannā vayasā ca mahīpate striya ādāya kāś cit sā jagāma vanam añjasā
english: Then, O lord of the earth, endowed with beauty and youth, she took some women with her and went straightway into the forest.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca sā tu nāvyāśramaṃ cakre rājakāryārthasiddhaye saṃdeśāc caiva nṛpateḥ svabuddhyā caiva bhārata
english: Lomaśa said: She fashioned a floating hermitage for the accomplishment of the king's purpose — both by the king's command and by her own wit, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nānāpuṣpaphalair vṛkṣaiḥ kṛtrimair upaśobhitam nānāgulmalatopetaiḥ svādukāmaphalapradaiḥ
english: It was adorned with artificial trees bearing various flowers and fruits, furnished with various shrubs and creepers that yielded sweet and desirable fruits.

sanskrit: atīva ramaṇīyaṃ tad atīva ca manoharam cakre nāvyāśramaṃ ramyam adbhutopamadarśanam
english: She made that floating hermitage exceedingly delightful and exceedingly charming — lovely and wondrous to behold.

sanskrit: tato nibadhya tāṃ nāvam adūre kāśyapāśramāt cārayām āsa puruṣair vihāraṃ tasya vai muneḥ
english: Then, having moored that vessel not far from the hermitage of Kāśyapa, she had men spy out the movements of that sage.

sanskrit: tato duhitaraṃ veśyā samādhāyetikṛtyatām dṛṣṭvāntaraṃ kāśyapasya prāhiṇod buddhisaṃmatām
english: Then the courtesan, having settled upon the plan and watching for an opportunity when Kāśyapa was away, sent her daughter — deemed wise — forward.

sanskrit: sā tatra gatvā kuśalā taponityasya saṃnidhau āśramaṃ taṃ samāsādya dadarśa tam ṛṣeḥ sutam
english: She, skilled in her craft, went there near where the perpetual ascetic dwelt, approached that hermitage, and beheld the son of the sage.

sanskrit: veśyovāca kaccin mune kuśalaṃ tāpasānāṃ; kaccic ca vo mūlaphalaṃ prabhūtam kaccid bhavān ramate cāśrame 'smiṃs; tvāṃ vai draṣṭuṃ sāṃpratam āgato 'smi
english: The courtesan said: "Are the ascetics well, O sage? Is your supply of roots and fruits abundant? Do you take pleasure in this hermitage? I have come just now to see you."

sanskrit: kaccit tapo vardhate tāpasānāṃ; pitā ca te kaccid ahīnatejāḥ kaccit tvayā prīyate caiva vipra; kaccit svādhyāyaḥ kriyate ṛśyaśṛṅga
english: "Do the austerities of the ascetics increase? Is your father of undiminished splendour? Does he take pleasure in you, O brāhmaṇa? Is Vedic recitation performed, O Ṛśyaśṛṅga?"

sanskrit: ṛśyaśṛṅga uvāca ṛddho bhavāñ jyotir iva prakāśate; manye cāhaṃ tvām abhivādanīyam pādyaṃ vai te saṃpradāsyāmi kāmād; yathādharmaṃ phalamūlāni caiva
english: Ṛśyaśṛṅga said: "You shine like a brilliant light, prosperous; I consider you worthy of reverence. I will gladly offer you water for your feet, as is proper, and also fruits and roots."

sanskrit: kauśyāṃ bṛsyām āssva yathopajoṣaṃ; kṛṣṇājinenāvṛtāyāṃ sukhāyām kva cāśramas tava kiṃ nāma cedaṃ; vrataṃ brahmaṃś carasi hi devavat tvam
english: "Sit at your ease on this silken mat covered with a black antelope skin for comfort. Where is your hermitage, and what is your name? And what vow do you practise, O brāhmaṇa, for you are like a god?"

sanskrit: veśyovāca mamāśramaḥ kāśyapaputra ramyas; triyojanaṃ śailam imaṃ pareṇa tatra svadharmo 'nabhivādanaṃ no; na codakaṃ pādyam upaspṛśāmaḥ
english: The courtesan said: "My hermitage is lovely, O son of Kāśyapa, beyond this hill at a distance of three leagues. There it is our custom not to receive reverence, nor do we accept water for washing of feet."

sanskrit: ṛśyaśṛṅga uvāca phalāni pakvāni dadāni te 'haṃ; bhallātakāny āmalakāni caiva parūṣakānīṅgudadhanvanāni; priyālānāṃ kāmakāraṃ kuruṣva
english: Ṛśyaśṛṅga said: "I will give you ripe fruits — marking-nut fruits and emblic myrobalans, parūṣaka berries and inguda fruits of the desert. Eat your fill of the priyāla nuts."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca sā tāni sarvāṇi visarjayitvā; bhakṣān mahārhān pradadau tato 'smai tāny ṛśyaśṛṅgasya mahārasāni; bhṛśaṃ surūpāṇi ruciṃ dadur hi
english: Lomaśa said: Rejecting all those offerings, she gave him precious delicacies instead. Those things, full of exquisite flavour, exceedingly beautiful in form, truly pleased the taste of Ṛśyaśṛṅga.

sanskrit: dadau ca mālyāni sugandhavanti; citrāni vāsāṃsi ca bhānumanti pānāni cāgryāṇi tato mumoda; cikrīḍa caiva prajahāsa caiva
english: She gave him fragrant garlands, bright and variegated garments, and excellent drinks; then she rejoiced, sported, and laughed.

sanskrit: sā kandukenāramatāsya mūle; vibhajyamānā phalitā lateva gātraiś ca gātrāṇi niṣevamāṇā; samāśliṣac cāsakṛt ṛśyaśṛṅgam
english: She played with a ball at his side, like a fruit-laden creeper swaying — pressing her limbs against his limbs, she embraced Ṛśyaśṛṅga repeatedly.

sanskrit: sarjān aśokāṃs tilakāṃś ca vṛkṣān; prapuṣpitān avanāmyāvabhajya vilajjamāneva madābhibhūtā; pralobhayām āsa sutaṃ maharṣeḥ
english: Bending down and breaking off the fully-flowering sarja, aśoka, and tilaka trees, as though overcome with intoxication and feigning bashfulness, she enticed the son of the great sage.

sanskrit: atharśyaśṛṅgaṃ vikṛtaṃ samīkṣya; punaḥ punaḥ pīḍya ca kāyam asya avekṣamāṇā śanakair jagāma; kṛtvāgnihotrasya tadāpadeśam
english: Then, having observed Ṛśyaśṛṅga stirred and having pressed his body again and again, she slowly departed, taking as pretext the maintenance of the sacred fire.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ gatāyāṃ madanena matto; vicetanaś cābhavad ṛśyaśṛṅgaḥ tām eva bhāvena gatena śūnyo; viniḥśvasann ārtarūpo babhūva
english: After she departed, Ṛśyaśṛṅga became overwhelmed by passion and bewildered; emptied of all feeling save longing for her, sighing and appearing distressed.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād dharipiṅgalākṣaḥ; praveṣṭito romabhirā nakhāgrāt svādhyāyavān vṛttasamādhiyukto; vibhāṇḍakaḥ kāśyapaḥ prādurāsīt
english: Then, after a moment, Vibhāṇḍaka Kāśyapa appeared — tawny-yellow-eyed, his body covered with hair to the tips of his nails, devoted to Vedic recitation and absorbed in the practice of vows.

sanskrit: so 'paśyad āsīnam upetya putraṃ; dhyāyantam ekaṃ viparītacittam viniḥśvasantaṃ muhur ūrdhvadṛṣṭiṃ; vibhāṇḍakaḥ putram uvāca dīnam
english: Approaching, he saw his son sitting alone, in meditation, with an agitated mind, sighing repeatedly with upward gaze; Vibhāṇḍaka addressed his son in a gentle tone.

sanskrit: na kalpyante samidhaḥ kiṃ nu tāta; kaccid dhutaṃ cāgnihotraṃ tvayādya sunirṇiktaṃ sruksruvaṃ homadhenuḥ; kaccit savatsā ca kṛtā tvayādya
english: "The kindling sticks are not being arranged — what is this, my son? Have you performed the agnihotra oblation today? Have the ladle and pouring-spoon been well cleaned? Has the ritual cow with her calf been tended today?"

sanskrit: na vai yathāpūrvam ivāsi putra; cintāparaś cāsi vicetanaś ca dīno 'timātraṃ tvam ihādya kiṃ nu; pṛcchāmi tvāṃ ka ihādyāgato 'bhūt
english: "You are not as you were before, my son — you are lost in thought and bewildered, exceedingly dejected here today. What is this? I ask you: who has come here today?"

sanskrit: ṛśyaśṛṅga uvāca ihāgato jaṭilo brahmacārī; na vai hrasvo nātidīrgho manasvī suvarṇavarṇaḥ kamalāyatākṣaḥ; sutaḥ surāṇām iva śobhamānaḥ
english: Ṛśyaśṛṅga said: "A matted-haired celibate student came here — neither short nor overly tall, mindful, golden in complexion, with eyes long as lotus petals, shining like the son of the gods."

sanskrit: samṛddharūpaḥ saviteva dīptaḥ; suśuklakṛṣṇākṣataraś cakoraiḥ nīlāḥ prasannāś ca jaṭāḥ sugandhā; hiraṇyarajjugrathitāḥ sudīrghāḥ
english: "Perfectly formed and radiant as the sun, with eyes clearer and whiter than even the cakora bird's — dark, lustrous, fragrant matted locks, braided with golden cords and very long."

sanskrit: ādhārarūpā punar asya kaṇṭhe; vibhrājate vidyud ivāntarikṣe dvau cāsya piṇḍāv adhareṇa kaṇṭham; ajātaromau sumanoharau ca
english: "On the neck, something serving as a necklace shines like lightning in the sky; and two rounded forms below the neck, hairless and most charming to the heart."

sanskrit: vilagnamadhyaś ca sa nābhideśe; kaṭiś ca tasyātikṛtapramāṇā tathāsya cīrāntaritā prabhāti; hiraṇmayī mekhalā me yatheyam
english: "Slender in the middle at the navel-region, yet the hips of extraordinary measure; and his girdle, shining through the bark garment, seemed to me like a girdle of gold."

sanskrit: anyac ca tasyādbhutadarśanīyaṃ; vikūjitaṃ pādayoḥ saṃprabhāti pāṇyoś ca tadvat svanavan nibaddhau; kalāpakāv akṣamālā yatheyam
english: "And another wondrous thing — a jingling at the feet was radiant, and likewise on the hands, making a sweet sound, bound there — like rosaries worn as armlets."

sanskrit: viceṣṭamānasya ca tasya tāni; kūjanti haṃsā sarasīva mattāḥ cīrāṇi tasyādbhutadarśanāni; nemāni tadvan mama rūpavanti
english: "And as he moved about, those things jingled like maddened swans on a lake. His bark garments were wondrous to behold — mine are not so beautiful as those."

sanskrit: vaktraṃ ca tasyādbhutadarśanīyaṃ; pravyāhṛtaṃ hlādayatīva cetaḥ puṃskokilasyeva ca tasya vāṇī; tāṃ śṛṇvato me vyathito 'ntarātmā
english: "And the face was wondrous to behold — the words spoken seemed to gladden the heart; and the voice like that of a male cuckoo — hearing it my inner self was moved and troubled."

sanskrit: yathā vanaṃ mādhavamāsi madhye; samīritaṃ śvasanenābhivāti tathā sa vāty uttamapuṇyagandhī; niṣevyamāṇaḥ pavanena tāta
english: "As a forest in the month of Mādhava wafts its scent in the middle when stirred by the breeze, so he breathed forth a fragrance of supreme purity when caressed by the wind, O father."

sanskrit: susaṃyatāś cāpi jaṭā vibhaktā; dvaidhīkṛtā bhānti samā lalāṭe karṇau ca citrair iva cakravālaiḥ; samāvṛtau tasya surūpavadbhiḥ
english: "And the matted locks, well-bound and parted, divided in two, gleamed evenly upon the forehead; and the ears were adorned with rings beautiful as painted wheels."

sanskrit: tathā phalaṃ vṛttam atho vicitraṃ; samāhanat pāṇinā dakṣiṇena tad bhūmim āsādya punaḥ punaś ca; samutpataty adbhutarūpam uccaiḥ
english: "And a round, variegated fruit — he struck it with his right hand; touching the ground again and again, it bounded up in a wondrous manner, high into the air."

sanskrit: tac cāpi hatvā parivartate 'sau; vāterito vṛkṣa ivāvaghūrṇaḥ taṃ prekṣya me putram ivāmarāṇāṃ; prītiḥ parā tāta ratiś ca jātā
english: "And striking it still, he turned about like a tree shaken by the wind; beholding him, who seemed to me like the son of the immortals, a great delight and joy arose in me, O father."

sanskrit: sa me samāśliṣya punaḥ śarīraṃ; jaṭāsu gṛhyābhyavanāmya vaktram vaktreṇa vaktraṃ praṇidhāya śabdaṃ; cakāra tan me 'janayat praharṣam
english: "He embraced my body, took hold of my matted locks, and bowed his face; pressing his mouth to my mouth, he made a sound — that produced in me the greatest delight."

sanskrit: na cāpi pādyaṃ bahu manyate 'sau; phalāni cemāni mayāhṛtāni evaṃvrato 'smīti ca mām avocat; phalāni cānyāni navāny adān me
english: "He thought nothing of the water for his feet, nor of these fruits I had brought; saying 'Such is my vow,' he gave me other fruits, fresh ones."

sanskrit: mayopayuktāni phalāni tāni; nemāni tulyāni rasena teṣām na cāpi teṣāṃ tvag iyaṃ yathaiṣāṃ; sārāṇi naiṣām iva santi teṣām
english: "Those fruits I ate — these here are not equal to those in flavour; nor is the skin of these like those, nor do these have the essence that those had."

sanskrit: toyāni caivātirasāni mahyaṃ; prādāt sa vai pātum udārarūpaḥ pītvaiva yāny abhyadhikaḥ praharṣo; mamābhavad bhūś caliteva cāsīt
english: "And waters of surpassing flavour that noble-formed one gave me to drink; having drunk them, a great joy arose in me — the very earth seemed to sway."

sanskrit: imāni citrāṇi ca gandhavanti; mālyāni tasyodgrathitāni paṭṭaiḥ yāni prakīryeha gataḥ svam eva; sa āśramaṃ tapasā dyotamānaḥ
english: "And these variegated fragrant garlands, unstrung from their silk threads, which he scattered here as he went to his own hermitage — he who blazes with austerity."

sanskrit: gatena tenāsmi kṛto vicetā; gātraṃ ca me saṃparitapyatīva icchāmi tasyāntikam āśu gantuṃ; taṃ ceha nityaṃ parivartamānam
english: "After he departed, I was made bewildered; my body seems to burn. I desire to go quickly to his side, and to have him ever moving here."

sanskrit: gacchāmi tasyāntikam eva tāta; kā nāma sā vratacaryā ca tasya icchāmy ahaṃ carituṃ tena sārdhaṃ; yathā tapaḥ sa caraty ugrakarmā
english: "I will go to his very side, O father — what is that vow he practises? I desire to practise it together with him, even as he performs that fierce austerity."

sanskrit: vibhāṇḍaka uvāca rakṣāṃsi caitāni caranti putra; rūpeṇa tenādbhutadarśanena atulyarūpāṇy atighoravanti; vighnaṃ sadā tapasaś cintayanti
english: Vibhāṇḍaka said: "These are demons roaming about, my son, in that wondrous form — of incomparable appearance, exceedingly terrible; they ever contrive obstacles to austerity."

sanskrit: surūparūpāṇi ca tāni tāta; pralobhayante vividhair upāyaiḥ sukhāc ca lokāc ca nipātayanti; tāny ugrakarmāṇi munīn vaneṣu
english: "Those beings of beautiful form, O son, entice sages in the forests by various stratagems, and cause them to fall from the worlds of blessedness — they of fierce and evil deeds."

sanskrit: na tāni seveta munir yatātmā; satāṃ lokān prārthayānaḥ kathaṃ cit kṛtvā vighnaṃ tāpasānāṃ ramante; pāpācārās tapasas tāpy apāpa
english: "A self-controlled sage seeking the worlds of the righteous should never associate with them in any way; those of evil conduct make sport of obstructing the austerities of ascetics — and they steal the heat of austerity."

sanskrit: asajjanenācaritāni putra; pāpāny apeyāni madhūni tāni mālyāni caitāni na vai munīnāṃ; smṛtāni citrojjvalagandhavanti
english: "These pleasures practised by the wicked, O son, are sweet but should not be tasted; and these garlands, bright and fragrant — they are not at all considered suitable for sages."

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca rakṣāṃsi tānīti nivārya putraṃ; vibhāṇḍakas tāṃ mṛgayāṃ babhūva nāsādayām āsa yadā tryaheṇa; tadā sa paryāvavṛte ''śramāya
english: Lomaśa said: Having restrained his son by saying "these are demons," Vibhāṇḍaka went off on a hunt; when he had not obtained game within three days, he then returned to the hermitage.

sanskrit: yadā punaḥ kāśyapo vai jagāma; phalāny āhartuṃ vidhinā śrāmaṇena tadā punar lobhayituṃ jagāma; sā veśayoṣā munim ṛśyaśṛṅgam
english: When Kāśyapa went again to gather fruits according to the rites of the forest-student, then again that courtesan went to entice the sage Ṛśyaśṛṅga.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva tām ṛśyaśṛṅgaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ; saṃbhrāntarūpo 'bhyapatat tadānīm provāca caināṃ bhavato ''śramāya; gacchāva yāvan na pitā mamaiti
english: The very moment he saw her, Ṛśyaśṛṅga was overjoyed; agitated in appearance, he ran toward her at once and spoke: "Let us go to your hermitage before my father comes."

sanskrit: tato rājan kāśyapasyaikaputraṃ; praveśya yogena vimucya nāvam pralobhayantyo vividhair upāyaiḥ; ājagmur aṅgādhipateḥ samīpam
english: Then, O king, having lured the sole son of Kāśyapa on board by stratagem, they set sail, and enticing him with various means, they came to the presence of the lord of the Aṅgas.

sanskrit: saṃsthāpya tām āśramadarśane tu; saṃtāritāṃ nāvam atīva śubhrām tīrād upādāya tathaiva cakre; rājāśramaṃ nāma vanaṃ vicitram
english: Having anchored the exceedingly bright vessel in view of the hermitage and taken it from the bank, the king likewise made a wondrous forest called the "Royal Hermitage."

sanskrit: antaḥpure taṃ tu niveśya rājā; vibhāṇḍakasyātmajam ekaputram dadarśa devaṃ sahasā pravṛṣṭam; āpūryamāṇaṃ ca jagaj jalena
english: When the king had settled the only son of Vibhāṇḍaka in the inner palace, he suddenly saw rain pour down, and the world filling with water.

sanskrit: sa lomapādaḥ paripūrṇakāmaḥ; sutāṃ dadāv ṛśyaśṛṅgāya śāntām krodhapratīkārakaraṃ ca cakre; gobhiś ca mārgeṣv abhikarṣaṇaṃ ca
english: That Lomapāda, his wish fulfilled, gave his daughter Śāntā to Ṛśyaśṛṅga; he also made amends for the wrong done, and had cattle drag ploughs along the roads.

sanskrit: vibhāṇḍakasyāvrajataḥ sa rājā; paśūn prabhūtān paśupāṃś ca vīrān samādiśat putragṛddhī maharṣir; vibhāṇḍakaḥ paripṛcched yadā vaḥ
english: For the approaching Vibhāṇḍaka, that king deployed abundant cattle and valiant herdsmen — eager for his son — so that when the great sage Vibhāṇḍaka should question you, they would answer:

sanskrit: sa vaktavyaḥ prāñjalibhir bhavadbhiḥ; putrasya te paśavaḥ karṣaṇaṃ ca kiṃ te priyaṃ vai kriyatāṃ maharṣe; dāsāḥ sma sarve tava vāci baddhāḥ
english: "He is to be told by you with folded hands: 'These cattle and this ploughing are your son's. What is pleasing to you, let it be done, great sage — we are all your servants, bound to your word.'"

sanskrit: athopāyāt sa muniś caṇḍakopaḥ; svam āśramaṃ mūlaphalāni gṛhya anveṣamāṇaś ca na tatra putraṃ; dadarśa cukrodha tato bhṛśaṃ saḥ
english: Then that sage of fierce wrath approached his own hermitage, carrying roots and fruits; searching but not finding his son there, he was greatly enraged.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa kopena vidīryamāṇa; āśaṅkamāno nṛpater vidhānam jagāma campāṃ pradidhakṣamāṇas; tam aṅgarājaṃ viṣayaṃ ca tasya
english: Then, bursting with fury and suspecting the king's contrivance, he marched toward Campā intent on burning that king of the Aṅgas and his kingdom.

sanskrit: sa vai śrāntaḥ kṣudhitaḥ kāśyapas tān; ghoṣān samāsāditavān samṛddhān gopaiś ca tair vidhivat pūjyamāno; rājeva tāṃ rātrim uvāsa tatra
english: Weary and hungry, Kāśyapa came to those prosperous cow-herding settlements; honoured duly by those cowherds as though he were a king, he spent that night there.
